ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all UBOs and directors against the French TRACFIN financial intelligence unit lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions regime, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic French asset-freeze lists; obligatory risk-based PEP detection in accordance with CMF Article L561-10 and AMF General Regulation; additional verification of PEP status persists for at least 12 months after public office termination under CMF Article R561-10-2; all screening outputs must be retained for five years post business-relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI Registre National des Entreprises / RNE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be drafted in Latin characters and subject to French-language rules under Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994 (Toubon Law); names in any non-Latin script must be transliterated into French-compatible Latin script for registry acceptance; the chosen corporate name must avoid confusion with existing trademarks and prior company names recorded in the INPI/RNE database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the INPI/RNE registry, file a formal written appeal with the competent Directeur Régional de l'INPI within two months of the notification, attaching the official rejection letter, corrected name proposal, and evidence of non-conflict with existing prior names/trademarks; if the administrative appeal remains unsuccessful, file an application within two months with the Paris Commercial Court or the competent Tribunal Judiciaire; alternative route: abandon the contested name and immediately reserve a cleared non-conflicting corporate name through the INPI trademark pre-reservation system, which resets the 30-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for SAS entities under Code de commerce Article L123-11-2 via an approved domiciliation company (entreprise de domiciliation), renewable for up to five years; however, an equity crowdfunding portal under EU Regulation 2020/1503 and AMF General Regulation must maintain genuine administrative and operational substance in France, including a permanent address for supervisory inspections and the availability of key officers, such that a pure virtual office without operational management capacity creates material regulatory non-compliance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high quantified risk of 30% probability of an unannounced on-site regulatory inspection during the first 12 operating months, driven by the special-license crowdfunding risk tier (ISIC 6499) and the AMF/ACPR joint supervisory practice for regulated digital investment intermediaries.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French Public Finances General Directorate; official tax administration portal: impots.gouv.fr; business taxpayer interface and e-filing via 'Espace Professionnel' and Chorus Pro.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, the statutory TIN (SIREN) and establishment ID (SIRET) are obtained automatically upon company registration with the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) within the jurisdiction of the registered office. The DGFiP subsequently issues the VAT identification number (n° TVA intracommunautaire) through the impots.gouv.fr professional portal after the CFE dossier is transmitted. Non-resident entities engaging in direct taxable supplies without a fixed establishment must complete the simplified registration regime under Article 286 ter of the CGI via the 'Service des impôts des entreprises', submitting proof of legal existence, power of attorney, expected activity, and a French fiscal representative only when required under applicable VAT rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a check-the-box classification system. An SAS is automatically subject to entity-level corporation income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) under Article 206-1 of the CGI. Available elections include the option to form a tax consolidation group under Article 223 A CGI where at least 95% control and a minimum one-year inclusion period are met, the option for group subsidiaries to use loss-absorption and integration equalisation, and the mandatory filing of excess-fragmentation and hybrid-mismatch notifications required under EU ATAD as transposed into French domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Under Article 293 B CGI, the French VAT exemption ('franchise en base de TVA') implies mandatory registration once annual turnover exceeds EUR 37,500 for services (the equity crowdfunding portal's core activity) or EUR 85,000 for goods. Increased 'seuil majoré' thresholds of EUR 41,000 for services and EUR 93,500 for goods apply where the immediately preceding year did not exceed the normal threshold. An entity may voluntarily register for VAT from its first taxable transaction even below these thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured electronic invoicing and e-reporting for domestic B2B transactions via accredited dematerialization platforms (PDPs) and the public portal Chorus Pro. Phased entry into force is 1 September 2026 for large and mid-sized enterprises and 1 September 2027 for small enterprises and micro-enterprises. E-reporting is mandatory for B2C sales and cross-border transaction data. The regime uses PEPPOL-like standards and API-based transmission to DGFiP, but France does not currently impose continuous transaction control with real-time fiscal clearance or Italian-style digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be zero-rated under Article 262-1 CGI if the physical export is proved, the goods leave the EU within the prescribed period, and the exporter retains evidence of the export declaration accepted by customs. For the equity crowdfunding portal's cross-border services, French VAT does not apply as a 0% rate; instead, B2B services supplied to non-EU business customers are outside the territorial scope under Articles 259 A and 259 B CGI, and B2C services supplied to non-EU consumers are generally outside French VAT where the effective use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU, with supporting documentation required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation) accepted and validated by French or EU customs authorities
Bill of Lading, CMR, Air Waybill, or equivalent transport document evidencing physical departure of goods from EU/EEA territory
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank credit advice, or SWIFT MT103 showing the export payment has been received and repatriated
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP audits export zero-rating claims strictly. Missing or contradictory proof that goods failed to leave the EU, or documentation indicating the exporter is not the true seller in substance, will trigger re-characterisation as a domestic taxable supply and assessment of 20% French VAT. For deliberate misstatements, concealment, or organised fraudulent practice, the taxpayer faces late-payment interest at 0.2% per month plus penalties up to 40% for bad faith and up to 80% for organised fraud, with a ten-year retrospective limitation period in fraud cases and possible criminal sanctions under Article 1741 CGI.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank and balance-of-payments statistical authority), with prudential supervision of credit institutions and ECSP/PSFP registrations by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); securities and crowdfunding conduct supervision by the Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF). The Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) administers exchange-control policy and foreign investment screening under the Code monétaire et financier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member and the euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account operations. There are no domestic exchange controls restricting inbound or outbound transfers, and profit remittance is unrestricted after ordinary tax and filing obligations are met. Dividends from a French SAS to non-resident shareholders are in principle subject to the 30% domestic withholding provided by Article 119 bis of the Code Général des Impôts, before treaty relief (generally ranging from 0% to 25%) or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption for qualifying corporate shareholders. The principal practical hurdles to capital mobility are the €12,500 per-counterparty monthly balance-of-payments notification obligation to Banque de France, EU sanctions and AML filtering, and the FDI screening regime under Articles L151-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier for activities falling within sensitive sectors or subject to certain foreign government ownership thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France does not impose surrender of export proceeds, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation timelines; a French SAS may freely retain in any currency all foreign trade proceeds and service revenue. Nonetheless, cross-border cash transactions in excess of €12,500 per counterparty per calendar month must be reported to Banque de France as balance-of-payments statistics, and payments involving a foreign State or non-cooperative jurisdiction may be subject to enhanced documentary orientation. Client funds collected by the crowdfunding platform under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 are segregated and are not treated as export proceeds for any surrender or conversion purpose.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Séquestre and Operational Account
Capital Escrow / Compte de Cantonnement and Operational Account
Treasury / Operational Account and FX Hedging Lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational treasury; Low for client-facing escrow under the ECSP/PSFP regime. A non-French EU electronic money institution (EMI) can passport into France under Directive 2009/110/EC and open an operational treasury account for the SAS. However, Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 requires crowdfunding client funds to be safeguarded by one or more credit institutions, or authorised payment/e-money institutions in segregated accounts, and de facto French ACPR guidance and bank counterparty practice require the underlying collection and escrow accounts to sit with a fully licensed French or EU credit institution. Offshore EMIs located outside the EEA cannot lawfully provide account services in France without a French or passporting licence, therefore an offshore EMI is viable only for ancillary disbursement routing, never for client-money custody or regulatory capital deposits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not statutorily mandated as remote video-identification is permitted under Article R561-9 of the Code monétaire et financier; in practice, for a high-risk crowdfunding SAS, first-tier French banks require at least one in-person interview at a French branch for the Président and the designated AML/Compliance Officer. The interview is supplemented by certified corporate documentation, UBO attestations, and presentation of the investor onboarding and funds segregation model. Non-resident decision-makers should expect a physical pre-onboarding validation meeting in France, and on exceptional occasions a visit to the platform's registered office; some institutions will accept a French-resident delegated signatory with a notarised power of attorney to satisfy the presence requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Crowdfunding platforms are treated as inherently high-risk due to large volumes of low-ticket public fund collection and possible exposure to money laundering and terrorist financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the final ACPR ECSP/PSFP registration certificate or AMF co-registration, the complete AML/CTF procedural manual, Tracfin-compliant internal control charter, investor and issuer risk-rating methodology, automated transaction-monitoring configuration, and audited evidence of client-fund segregation under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opaque beneficial-ownership chain or beneficial owners resident in jurisdictions with tax/AML transparency deficiencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn UBO declaration filed with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs via Infogreffe, notarised ownership chain from every natural-person UBO holding at least 25% of the SAS, apostilled passports and national residence proof, tax residence certificates, bank references from FATF-compliant institutions, and, where applicable, documentary evidence of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: expected high-velocity mixed retail inflows that impose on the bank an obligation to apply per-investor sanctions and PEP screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor e-KYC journey including identity verification, sanctions/PEP screening through systemic sweeps, investor contribution caps and concordance checks, enhanced due diligence procedures for contributions above €10,000, contractual commitment to deliver, upon request, structured investor files enabling the bank's own screening, and confirmation that all client funds are denominated solely in EUR.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident founders and directors of the French SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport copies, sworn French translations of statutory documents, proof of a bona fide French registered office (lease, insurance, utility), notarised powers of attorney for French-resident bank signatories, criminal record extracts issued less than three months prior in the State of residence, and a bank reference letter drawn by the directors' primary bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: latent risk that the SAS operates unauthorised payment services by collecting or transmitting crowdfunding funds directly.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed escrow agreement with a licensed French or EU credit institution, executed processing agreements with regulated EU payment institutions or EMIs (for example Mangopay, Lemonway, or Stripe) including their authorisation references, and a business-model statement expressly limiting the SAS to MiFID/crowdfunding intermediation, excluding any own-account dealing, deposit-taking, or custody beyond the settlement transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital injections must be routed as SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA shareholders) from the shareholder's personal or corporate account to the SAS operational EUR account, with a structured remittance referencing the corporate approval (P.V. d'Assemblée), SIREN identifier, and the Banque de France balance-of-payments category 'Investissements directs - création/augmentation de capital'. Where monthly cumulative cross-border flows exceed €12,500, the SAS must file with its French bank the Banque de France declaration of change (capital transaction form) before settlement. Verification at the bank requires the certified capital-increase resolution, updated UBO attestation, and a capital certificate signed by the Président; funds must originate from the account of the same legal entity as the subscribing shareholder in order to satisfy French AML traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR disbursements to French or EEA investee companies shall be executed by SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) with full structured creditor remittance information, or by SEPA Instant Credit Repayment (SCT) for urgent milestone payments. Non-EEA trade settlements shall be executed via SWIFT MT103 with selected purpose codes and complete payer/payee structured data required by Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (Travel Rule). For conditional payments dependent on subscription milestones or share issuance, commercially defensible rails are irrevocable documentary credits under ICC UCP 600 or bank-secured escrow release instructions conditioned upon evidence of share subscription; all amounts must clear exclusively through the segregated client-assets account so that platform treasury funds are not co-mingled with investor funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward FX contracts in major pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) documented under ISDA 2002 or the French Code de Change framework with an authorized credit institution
Over-the-counter vanilla currency options purchased to hedge genuine commercial exposure, with no net option-writing or speculative premium harvesting
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCCY/CCIRS) used to match non-EUR borrowings or contractual receivables
Rolling FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term liquidity management of recurring non-EUR receipts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted-settlement currencies, strictly supported by demonstrated underlying exposure and executed by an EU-authorized credit institution under EMIR margin and transaction-reporting obligations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual beneficial ownership declaration to RCS; update required within 30 days of changes in shareholdings or control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized enterprises may apply the 15% reduced rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per 12-month period, subject to qualifying conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. The standard 25% rate applies above that threshold. Certain qualifying new businesses and research and development activities may access separate, conditional incentives; eligibility and interaction with other aid must be verified.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual offset cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. A one-year carryback may be elected, generally capped at EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) professional tax portal using EDI-TDFC or the applicable online filing service. Attach the applicable corporate tax return schedules (liasse fiscale), generally Forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD under the normal regime or Forms 2033-A-SD to 2033-G-SD under the simplified regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with the final balance settled separately. A company meeting the statutory low-tax-liability exception may be exempt from instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second working day following 1 May. The final corporate tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 15 May. Tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, SIREN, registered office, tax office, activity, accounting-period start and end dates, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not replace the French SAS as the taxpayer. Report the French SAS's registered details and French accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable result after reconciling accounting profit or loss with tax adjustments and applying relevant deduction, limitation, and loss rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to the French SAS. Do not report a foreign shareholder's separate income as the SAS's income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute IS at the applicable rate and report eligible tax credits, reductions, and other amounts using the return and its schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only incentives for which the French company meets the substantive and filing conditions; retain supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Liasse fiscale: Forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD or 2033-A-SD to 2033-G-SD
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the applicable balance sheet, income statement, tax reconciliation, fixed-asset, provisions, and other required accounting and tax schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French accounting and tax rules to the SAS's books. Disclose related-party transactions and tax adjustments where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD: foreign tax and international transaction disclosures, where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable disclosures and related forms, including transfer-pricing and cross-border reporting schedules where statutory thresholds or transaction rules are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess French documentation and reporting obligations by reference to the French entity, its group, and its transactions; non-resident ownership does not itself exempt the SAS.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% where the return is not filed within 30 days after a formal notice, and potentially 80% in cases such as concealed activity or abuse of rights. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge plus late-payment interest, currently 0.20% per month, subject to applicable statutory rules. Inaccurate returns may incur additional penalties depending on fault, deliberate conduct, or fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: A 25% domestic withholding rate generally applies to dividends paid by a French company to non-residents, subject to reductions or exemptions under an applicable tax treaty or EU law. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction, beneficial ownership, and participation conditions. Dividends paid to eligible EU parent companies may qualify for the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, subject to its conditions and anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the beneficial owner should provide the French payer with the applicable French treaty relief form and a valid tax residence certificate issued by the competent authority in the residence jurisdiction. The payer applies the reduced rate or exemption only when the statutory documentation and substantive conditions are satisfied; otherwise, domestic withholding generally applies and the recipient may seek a refund using the prescribed French reclaim procedure. Confirm beneficial ownership, holding-period and minimum-participation conditions, limitation-on-benefits provisions, and anti-abuse rules. A residence certificate does not itself establish treaty entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% French withholding, subject to a lower treaty rate or a qualifying EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding, subject to exceptions, including payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions and specified anti-abuse or domestic-law cases; the domestic rate may reach 75% for certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions. Treaty rates and exemptions depend on the recipient, beneficial ownership, payment characterization, and applicable conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A French Local File and Master File are generally required for entities or French tax groups meeting the statutory threshold of EUR 400 million in annual turnover or gross assets, or belonging to a group meeting specified EUR 400 million thresholds or control conditions. Separate simplified transfer-pricing reporting obligations may apply to qualifying entities and certain transactions; the applicable threshold and reporting scope should be checked for the relevant year. Documentation must be available to the tax authorities upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. French tax rules nevertheless permit challenges to artificial arrangements, sham transactions, abuse of law, and arrangements lacking commercial substance. Transfer-pricing outcomes must reflect the actual functions performed, assets used, and risks controlled. For a regulated crowdfunding portal, maintain evidence of French decision-making, personnel, operational capability, risk control, and the actual performance of licensed activities; tax substance does not replace applicable financial-services authorization requirements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses, maintaining false accounts, or knowingly submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessments, late-payment interest, and surcharges may apply. Tax fraud may result in criminal penalties, including imprisonment and substantial fines; penalties depend on the offence, amount, and circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for company tax debts. Personal criminal liability may arise from their own participation or complicity. Statutory tax collection liability may apply where a director's fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated tax non-compliance makes collection impossible, subject to judicial determination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing misstatement and undocumented related-party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices, allocating profits inconsistently with functions and risks, failing to provide required documentation, or omitting required cross-border transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust taxable profits, assess tax, interest, and penalties, and impose specific documentation-related fines under the applicable rules. The amount depends on the breach and statutory calculation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability only where a separate statutory basis or their own criminal conduct is established; a transfer-pricing adjustment alone does not pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a crowdfunding service or offering regulated investment services without the required French or EU authorization, registration, or passporting rights, including handling client funds outside permitted arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include injunctions, cessation of activity, administrative sanctions, financial penalties, and criminal liability under the applicable financial-services legislation. The precise sanction depends on the activity and authorization breached.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face personal administrative or criminal proceedings for their own participation. Limited liability is not a defense to personal offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement required customer due diligence, beneficial-owner screening, transaction monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting, or asset-freezing controls, or knowingly processing prohibited transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative and criminal sanctions, fines, activity restrictions, and asset-freezing measures may apply under French and EU law. Sanctions and liability are fact-specific and may be severe.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for their own acts or omissions where the statutory elements are met. Corporate status does not shield an individual from personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other reportable cross-border amounts without timely withholding, declaration, payment, or adequate support for treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be liable for the unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, surcharges, and applicable penalties. Improper treaty relief may be denied and withholding recovered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically personally liable for withholding-tax debts; personal exposure may arise under statutory collection rules or for their own fraudulent or criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a company or transaction lacking genuine commercial purpose to conceal beneficial ownership, mischaracterize income, obtain treaty benefits improperly, or evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may deny tax benefits, recharacterize transactions, reassess tax, and impose interest and penalties. Fraud, money laundering, or other offences may trigger separate criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability requires a statutory basis or proof of personal participation in an offence. Fraudulent conduct may support criminal prosecution and, where legal conditions are met, personal collection liability; travel restrictions are not an automatic tax consequence.
